author: Brian Wilson
releaseNotes: 1.31.0 — A room too big to finish on one charge is no longer skipped forever. 1.30.0's check refuses to start a room the battery can't cover, but a large room whose estimate exceeds 100% could never satisfy that — it would have dropped out of rotation permanently and silently, sitting on "already due" with nothing but a log line. Close to happening in practice: a 37-minute room needs ~90% at the drain rate learned so far and crosses 100% if that rate rises about 13%, which one carpeted run at high suction could do. Such a room is now started once the battery reaches 95% and the vacuum's own charge-and-resume finishes it, and the app page names any room in that state since it's the clearest sign it's worth splitting into smaller zones in the Wyze app. Also documents the Rule Machine rule for re-cleaning after a recharge while nobody is home, including the conditions that keep it from running overnight or past a full bin during a long absence. 1.30.1 — Multi-vacuum fix, found by auditing whether two vacuums can interfere with each other. Hubitat keys pending runIn() jobs by handler method name and overwrites by default, so with more than one vacuum the second one to schedule a rotation-sweep continuation silently cancelled the first's, stalling that vacuum's sweep a room early. Because pollAllVacuums() polls every vacuum in one execution, their callbacks land milliseconds apart, so two sweeps advancing in the same poll cycle would have collided every time rather than occasionally. Those jobs now schedule with overwrite:false. Single-vacuum setups were never affected. 1.30.0 — Rotation no longer starts a room the battery can't cover. This is not a second opinion on Wyze's own ~8% return-to-dock threshold, which is left entirely alone: that decides when to head home mid-run, while this decides whether setting out is worth it at all, which the firmware never asks. Confirmed live: a sweep dispatched a room at 8% battery and the vacuum never acted on the command — not on the first try, nor on the automatic retry — costing a dispatch, a retry, a spurious "never started" alert, and a room left looking untouched. The requirement is the room's own learned clean time multiplied by how fast this vacuum actually drains (measured from real runs, same as room times are, starting from 2.3%/min), plus a 10% reserve so it isn't finishing right at Wyze's threshold. Skipped rooms stay due and get picked up on the next trigger, and a multi-room batch is trimmed to whatever does fit rather than skipped outright. On by default, with a per-vacuum opt-out; cleanRooms(), room buttons and Learning Mode always run regardless. 1.29.1 — Fixes the switch attribute latching on, a regression from 1.29.0. When a dispatched room-clean is given up on (the vacuum acknowledged the command but never acted on it, even after the automatic retry), the run was cleared but the rotation sweep flag was left set — and since 1.29.0 reads that flag as "work outstanding," the switch stayed on indefinitely with the vacuum sitting idle on its dock. Confirmed live: a dispatch at 8% battery was never acted on, given up on 11 minutes later, and the switch was still on two hours afterwards. Every path that ends a sweep now clears all of its state through one helper, and a safety net clears a sweep flag found set with nothing running, queued, or cleaning. 1.29.0 — The switch attribute now stays on while a job is still outstanding, not just while the vacuum is physically moving. A job that runs the battery down leaves the vacuum docked and charging with every intention of resuming, but the switch used to flip off the moment cleaning stopped — which breaks the common on = clean next rooms / off = dock wiring, because the switch is already off when someone gets home and their "turn it off" automation has nothing to turn off, while the pending job resumes later anyway. Turning the switch off (or calling dock()/pause()) now also genuinely cancels a job that's paused for charging: the run is closed out, its rooms stay due rather than being credited, and if the vacuum starts up again on its own afterwards it's sent straight back to the dock — regardless of the "Don't let it auto-resume" setting, since an explicit stop already says what you want. 1.28.0 — New per-vacuum option, "Don't let it auto-resume" (under Low Battery Protection). When a job runs the battery down, the vacuum docks itself, charges, and then restarts that job on its own at whatever time charging happens to finish — confirmed live: an "everyone left" trigger started a rotation run at 5:57pm, the sweep advanced to the next room at 6:44pm on a 15% battery, that room ran flat at 6% by 6:51pm, and the vacuum restarted it itself at 8:35pm with everyone home again. The job is app-dispatched but the restart is the vacuum's own call, so a "dock when someone gets home" automation has nothing to catch — it fires on arrival, long before the firmware picks the job back up. With this on, a self-restarted job is sent straight back to the dock and the room stays pending for the next rotation, keeping its learned clean time. Off by default, preserving the existing finish-the-job behavior. 1.27.0 — Interrupting a room clean (dock()/pause()/off(), e.g. an automation firing when someone comes home) now sends its own notification saying what stopped it and how far in -- previously it reported as "finished cleaning," which was wrong twice over: a room cut short at minute 3 of 35 was fully credited as cleaned (dropping it from rotation for a whole cycle) and had its learned clean time overwritten with the truncated value, skewing future time-budget runs. A commanded stop is no longer treated as a finish. Multi-room batches still credit whichever rooms got their full time before the interruption. 1.26.0 — Better handling of cleans started outside Hubitat (from the Wyze app, the vacuum's own schedule, or its button), which this app detects and reports on like any other run. Two fixes from a live 2-zone Wyze-app clean: (1) such a run used to be announced as "started cleaning: whole house", which was untrue -- Wyze doesn't report which rooms/zones an externally-started run picked, so it now says so plainly, and "whole house" is claimed only when this app's own start() command kicked the run off. (2) When a job pauses at critically low battery and auto-resumes hours later (mode 11), the resume used to fire a second "started cleaning" notification as if it were a brand-new run -- it now reports it as resuming the same job, matching the finish-notification suppression added in 1.24.0.
